scope: Japji retained-learning preservation, published old-writer fixture, backup and failure behavior; synthetic records only

checks.name: An unknown saved note is kept in full with its original identifier
Unknown bookmarks are kept separately while recognized bookmarks still work
A reflection beyond the editing limit is retained without truncation
Legacy section and occurrence notes that collide are both preserved
Repeated reads neither duplicate retained entries nor lose their contents
Known notes and reading controls remain usable with retained items present
A stale tab keeps newly retained items from the latest stored record
Export and restore to an empty browser keeps every retained note and bookmark
Import merges both sets of retained notes without replacing conflicting text
Malformed retained-learning fields refuse writes and preserve the original raw record
Invalid non-text notes refuse normalization rather than silently disappearing
New write archives retained items before an old tab can replace the v2 record
Archive is persisted even when a previously unseen unknown note is opened before any main write
Export after an old overwrite carries the independent archive and restores it to a new browser
Restoring a retained archive alone keeps current notes and merges the retained records
If writing the separate archive fails, the original primary record is not replaced
Damaged archive refuses new writes and is exported byte for byte
Failed primary write during import rolls back the archive without losing earlier retained items
An ordinary reader without retained items does not create an archive
The actual published normalizer and shared writer cannot erase the new separate archive
